title: Rubio Calls Aoun & Netanyahu on June 1; US Proposes Phased De-escalation Plan Ahead of Lebanon-Israel Round 4 Washington Talks (June 2–3)
detail: June 1, 2026 — Secretary of State Marco Rubio conducted separate telephone calls with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on June 1 to prepare both parties for the upcoming Round 4 political-track talks in Washington, scheduled for June 2–3. According to Pakistan Today, Rubio tabled a phased de-escalation proposal as a framework for the discussions: in Phase 1, Hezbollah would cease all offensive operations against Israel; in exchange, Israel would refrain from further escalation in the greater Beirut area. The proposal is designed to stabilize the security environment sufficiently for the political-track talks to address the core structural issues — border demarcation, IDF withdrawal timeline from southern Lebanon, LAF deployment to the south, and long-term Hezbollah disarmament from the Litani line. Round 4 follows directly from the May 29 Pentagon security track meeting in which Brigadier General Georges Rizkallah led a Lebanese military delegation of 6 officers in the first military-to-military bilateral of the process. The June 2–3 talks are the next critical milestone in the process, with the 45-day ceasefire extension (in force since May 17) counting down to its ~June 29 expiry. Israel is represented in the political track by Yechiel Leiter, Lebanon by Simon Karam. Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem remains opposed to the direct talks format and has urged the Lebanese government to withdraw from the Washington process. The core impasse — Israeli insistence on verified Hezbollah disarmament south of the Litani before full IDF withdrawal vs. Lebanon's demand for unconditional IDF withdrawal first — has not been resolved.

title: US-Iran Deal Day 4 Unsigned: Trump Returns Amended MOU Drafts Seeking Stricter Nuclear Terms; IAEA Reports Record Iran HEU Stockpile
detail: June 1, 2026 — The US-Iran nuclear and Hormuz agreement confirmed tentatively by CNN on May 28 remains unsigned entering its fourth day. On June 1, President Trump sent back amended drafts of the memorandum of understanding, seeking stricter nuclear commitments from Tehran and expanded provisions governing Strait of Hormuz reopening guarantees and verification protocols. The amended drafts effectively extend the timeline for any formal signing by at least another week, according to reporting tracking the negotiation. Compounding the diplomatic pressure, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported on May 31 that Iran had amassed a record amount of military-grade enriched uranium — adding urgency to the US demand for enhanced HEU disposal provisions in the Phase 2 nuclear talks framework. The core MOU framework under negotiation: Phase 1 = Iran clears mines from the Strait, Hormuz reopens with no tolls, US lifts the naval blockade, sanctions waivers enable Iranian oil sales to resume; Phase 2 = 60-day nuclear negotiations on enrichment suspension limits and HEU stockpile removal under IAEA verification. The Strait of Hormuz enters Day 4 of the post-tentative-agreement period still physically closed — approximately 750 vessels remain trapped, approximately $6 billion per month in Iranian oil exports blocked, and US gasoline prices holding at approximately $4.48/gallon (Week 14 of closure). General Asim Munir of Pakistan continues as the principal back-channel intermediary connecting the US negotiating team (Vance, Witkoff, Kushner) with Iran's side. The congressional opposition bloc — 52 senators and 177 House members who wrote to Trump on May 14 opposing any deal permitting Iranian enrichment — continues to constrain the domestic political space for a formal announcement. Both sides are assessed as negotiating in earnest but the gap between 'tentative agreement' and a signed deal is proving more stubborn than VP Vance suggested on May 28 when he acknowledged only 'a couple of language points' remained.

title: Colombia ELN Election Ceasefire Holds Into Day 2; Cepeda and De la Espriella Begin June 21 Runoff Campaigns With Peace Architecture at Center
detail: June 1, 2026 — The ELN's 4-day election ceasefire (midnight May 30 through midnight June 2) continues holding on its second day with no significant violations reported. The ceasefire covers the May 31 first-round election and the immediate post-voting stabilization period, and security forces confirm the calm atmosphere persisting through June 1. Presidential candidates Iván Cepeda (Pacto Histórico, ~44-45% first round) and Abelardo De la Espriella (conservative, ~31%) have begun their June 21 runoff campaigns with Colombia's peace architecture as the defining axis of competition. Cepeda — a human rights lawyer and senator who built his political career around accountability for military 'false positives' and FARC-era abuses — has pledged to immediately restart ELN negotiations (suspended since January 2025 after the Catatumbo massacre), continue the JEP transitional justice system, and reopen FARC-EMC (Mordisco faction) talks on the basis of the 2016 accord. De la Espriella, who holds the consolidated support of Paloma Valencia's Democratic Center voters (~14% first round) and other conservative factions, has pledged to immediately terminate all negotiations with armed groups and pursue a military-first security approach. Crisis Group's May 2026 assessment 'Colombia's Polls Mark a Forking Path' notes the right-wing consolidation dynamic could make De la Espriella the June 21 runoff favorite despite losing the first round. The JEP continues operating independently of presidential politics — its macro-cases (including 'false positives') will proceed regardless of who wins June 21. The FARC-EMC and ELN remain outside any formal negotiating framework. Former President Petro's 'Total Peace' initiative, which saw ELN talks collapse January 2025 and FARC-EMC disengage citing unfulfilled 2016 accord obligations, formally ends with Petro's term on election day.
